clue.text: Before onset of thunderstorm, put on Basque's head?

definitions.text: Before onset of thunderstorm, put on Basque's head?

indicators.note: the following letters are put on, after, the Basque's opening letter in this across entry
the head of the word Basque's is its opening letter, picked out here

parts.note: ere is an old word meaning before

indicators.note: the onset of a storm is its start, so the word's first letter is taken

explanation.surface: Advice to a Basque to cover up before a storm breaks.
explanation.walkthrough: B (Basque's head) has ERE ('Before') and T ('onset of thunderstorm') put on after it; the whole clue also describes what a Basque might wear in bad weather.
explanation.definitionFit: The flat woollen cap is traditional Basque headgear, the thing a Basque would put on.

clue.text: Poor cricket side accepting a lot of money for the sport

parts.note: bad means poor in quality
a mint is a vast sum of money
the on side is the leg side of a cricket field

explanation.surface: A weak cricket team takes a big payment to switch sports.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the field is split into the off side and the on (leg) side.
explanation.definitionFit: Badminton is a racket game played with a shuttlecock over a high net.

clue.text: Solution for one wanting to change the locks

definitions.text: Solution for one wanting to change the locks

parts.words: Solution for one wanting to change the locks
parts.note: locks are tresses of hair, not door fastenings, and the solution is a liquid hair tint

explanation.surface: Advice for someone whose door locks need replacing.
explanation.definitionFit: A rinse is a temporary hair dye washed through the hair.

clue.text: Retaliatory blow small creature gives bird

parts.note: from tit for tat, a tit is a blow given in return
a mouse is a small creature

explanation.surface: A creature hits back at a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: Titmouse is the fuller name for the tit, a small songbird.

clue.text: Persistent blemish? Taken to court about that

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the court word goes round the blemish word

parts.note: to be taken to court is to be sued
a stain is a blemish

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a mark is lasting, then is sued over it.
explanation.definitionFit: Sustained effort is persistent, kept up without a break.

clue.text: Money paid for naval equipment

explanation.surface: A budget for a navy's gear.
explanation.definitionFit: Subs abbreviates both subscriptions and submarines.

clue.text: Weather set for a storm? That'll do for ducks!

indicators.note: being set for a storm means about to be thrown into turmoil, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Wet weather on the way, and a cheerful remark that ducks will enjoy it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ducks' is a British term of endearment, like love, so the definition names a loved one.
explanation.definitionFit: A loved one may be addressed as duck in parts of England, just as with darling.

clue.text: Graduate's rewritten manual

definitions.note: read as 'graduate is', the 's a link to the wordplay

indicators.note: rewritten means written out again differently, so the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A graduate has revised a handbook.
explanation.definitionFit: An alumna is a female former student of a college or university.

clue.text: It's about the ultimate in ill-repute — and no Conservative should accept that

definitions.text: It's about the ultimate in ill-repute — and no Conservative should accept that

indicators.note: accepting means taking in, so the party word contains the rest

parts.note: a Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party

indicators.note: about means around, so it goes round the final letter

parts.note: the word it, the 's a link

indicators.note: the ultimate letter of a word is its last

explanation.surface: A scandal so disreputable that no Tory should tolerate it.
explanation.walkthrough: Read whole, the clue also describes the answer: a bad name no party member wants. 'the ultimate in' takes the final E of 'ill-repute'.
explanation.definitionFit: Notoriety means being famous for something bad, a poor reputation.

clue.text: Black and blue?

definitions.meaning: soiled, grimy or dark with grime
smutty or indecent, as in a blue joke

explanation.surface: A bruise is being described.
explanation.definitionFit: Dirty means grimy and also obscene, as blue jokes are.

clue.text: Town's not very colourful and unlikely to change

definitions.note: read as 'town is', the 's a link to the wordplay

parts.note: dun is a dull greyish-brown colour
stable means steady, not liable to change

explanation.surface: A dull, unchanging place is being described.
explanation.walkthrough: DUNSTABLE is a market town in Bedfordshire, England.
explanation.definitionFit: Dunstable is a market town in Bedfordshire, north of London.

clue.text: Complete fool losing his head

indicators.note: losing his head means the fool word drops its opening letter

parts.note: nutter is British slang for a crazy person or fool

explanation.surface: A complete idiot has lost his head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing his head' takes the N off NUTTER.
explanation.definitionFit: Utter as an adjective means total or absolute, as in utter nonsense.

clue.text: Reserve top seats at the opera, getting a good store of champagne?

parts.note: ice is coolness of manner, reserve
a box is a private compartment of the best seats in a theatre or opera house

explanation.surface: Booking the best opera seats and stocking up on champagne.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reserve' looks like a verb meaning book; it is the noun, coolness of manner, giving ICE.
explanation.definitionFit: An icebox keeps things cold, a good place for chilling bubbly wine.

clue.text: Mean, pinching artist's fish

indicators.note: pinching means holding tight, so the mean word grips the artist

parts.note: stingy means mean with money
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: A tightfisted person is stealing a painter's fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pinching' looks like stealing; here it means gripping, so the artist sits inside the mean word. RA stands for a Royal Academician.
explanation.definitionFit: The flat ray with a venomous tail spine is a kind of fish.

clue.text: Opposing or supporting check on social worker?

parts.note: pro means in favour of
a test is a check
an ant is a worker in a social insect colony

explanation.surface: Someone for or against vetting a social worker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'social worker' looks like a care professional; it is the ant, a worker in a social insect colony.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective originally meant protesting, raising objections.

clue.text: A nuisance interrupting attempts to supply wall decorations

indicators.note: interrupting means breaking into, so these letters go inside the attempts word

parts.note: tries are attempts
a pest is a nuisance

explanation.surface: An annoying person keeps getting in the way of efforts to decorate.
explanation.definitionFit: Woven hangings with pictures were traditionally hung on walls as decoration.

clue.text: Victim mostly soft? One's appearance is deceptive

indicators.note: mostly means most but not all, so the word loses its last letter

parts.note: prey is a victim
tender means soft

explanation.surface: A gullible victim is fooled by a fraud.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' cuts PREY to PRE.
explanation.definitionFit: A pretender puts on a false show, claiming to be what they are not.

clue.text: Composer runs in to ask for notes, perhaps

indicators.note: in means the runs letter goes inside the asking word

parts.note: to beg is to ask for money, banknotes for example
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A composer dashes in requesting musical notes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'notes' suggests music; here they are banknotes, which a beggar asks for.
explanation.definitionFit: Alban Berg was an Austrian composer of the Second Viennese School.

clue.text: Soldier re-reading novel

indicators.note: novel means new, so the letters take a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: A soldier is reading a novel again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' looks like a book being read; it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A grenadier is a soldier, originally one who threw grenades.

clue.text: Game in swallowing tablet up? That can get you a sweet

indicators.note: up means read upwards in this down entry, so the whole is reversed
swallowing means taking inside, so the game contains the tablet

parts.note: pool is a cue game
a pill is a tablet

explanation.surface: Gulping pills during a game might earn you a treat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses POPILLOL, the tablet inside the game, in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A lollipop is a hard sweet on a stick.

clue.text: Spanish city backed this festival

indicators.note: backed means turned back, so the city name is read from its end

parts.note: Leon is a city in northern Spain

explanation.surface: A Spanish city sponsored a festival.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backed' looks like supported; it means reversed.
explanation.definitionFit: Noel is another name for Christmas, the festival.

clue.text: Poetry set originally with English printing-plate

indicators.note: originally means in an original, new way, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A poetry collection with English text is printed from a plate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'originally' signals the anagram of POETRY SET, giving STEREOTYP, then E for English.
explanation.definitionFit: A stereotype was a solid metal plate cast from set type, used for printing.

clue.text: Seaport some passed on heading North

indicators.note: heading north means travelling upwards in this down entry, so the letters read backwards
some means part of the following words, so the letters lie within them

explanation.surface: Some travellers passed through on the way north.
explanation.walkthrough: Inside 'passed on' read backwards are ODESSA.
explanation.definitionFit: Odessa is a major Black Sea port in Ukraine.

clue.text: Excess is something we may celebrate in love poems

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, which looks like the letter O

indicators.note: in means the party word sits inside the poems word

parts.note: verse means poems
a do is a party, an event people celebrate

explanation.surface: Too much of something is celebrated in love poetry.
explanation.walkthrough: Love as O is a tennis score; DO is a British word for a party.
explanation.definitionFit: An overdose is too much of a drug, an excessive amount taken.

clue.text: Total lack of pace after introduction of zero vitality

indicators.note: after introduction of means the lack of pace comes after the zero is introduced first

parts.note: zero looks like the letter O
zero miles per hour, O MPH, means standing still

explanation.surface: No speed at all once the zero is introduced: no energy.
explanation.definitionFit: Oomph is slang for energy and vigour.

clue.text: Almost all headgear backed with a woolly fabric

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the last letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: taken as written before trimming

indicators.note: backed means reversed, so the headgear is read backwards

parts.note: a cap is headgear

explanation.surface: Nearly all the hats are lined with wool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Almost' drops the last L from ALL; 'backed' turns CAP into PAC.
explanation.definitionFit: Alpaca is cloth woven from the wool of the South American animal.

clue.text: Benefit obtained by withholding name from agreement

indicators.note: withholding means keeping back, so the name letter is taken out

parts.note: assent is agreement

explanation.surface: An advantage gained by keeping a name out of a deal.
explanation.definitionFit: An asset is a useful quality or advantage, a benefit.

clue.text: Leading player sneakily leaves his side, wanting a rise

indicators.note: a rise in this down entry means the letters are read upwards, reversed

parts.note: to rat is to desert one's side, so he rats

explanation.surface: A top player defects from his team, wanting a pay rise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wanting a rise' looks like a pay demand; it reverses the letters upward in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: The star is the lead performer or best player.

clue.text: His golden handshake not wanted? Stupid to return it, on reflection

indicators.note: on reflection means mirrored, so each word is read backwards

parts.note: dim means stupid
it is a slang term for sex appeal, abbreviated SA

explanation.surface: A man spurns a redundancy payout, then thinks giving it back is foolish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on reflection' turns DIM to MID and SA to AS. A golden handshake is a large leaving payment; this king's touch turned all to gold, so a handshake was unwelcome.
explanation.definitionFit: The mythical king turned everything he touched to gold, so his handshake gilded people.

clue.text: Hint on a new wine for hors d'oeuvres

indicators.note: on means placed after, so the hint goes after the a-new letters

parts.note: a tip is a hint
Asti is a sparkling Italian wine

explanation.surface: A suggestion to start a meal with a new wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Antipasti are Italian starters served before the main course.

clue.text: Heaven, hopefully, making man beam? Ecstasy found therein

parts.note: he stands for a man

indicators.note: found therein means found inside the beam word

parts.note: a rafter is a roof beam
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A man gets high on a drug and imagines paradise.
explanation.definitionFit: The afterlife is where people hope to reach heaven.

clue.text: Wimsey, say, getting grip on heart of mystery?

definitions.text: Wimsey, say, getting grip on heart of mystery?

indicators.note: getting a grip on something means holding it within, so the lord's word surrounds the middle letter

parts.note: Lord ... Wimsey is a lord, a peer

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its central letter, here the fourth of seven

explanation.surface: Dorothy L Sayers's sleuth starts to solve a puzzle.
explanation.walkthrough: Wimsey is Dorothy L Sayers's aristocratic detective; as a peer he grips T, the centre of 'mystery', and his first name is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Lord Peter Wimsey's given name is the detective's forename.
